objects.original: The companion prerequisite concerns a normalized full-space Gibbs law, a completed smooth gradient graph, and weighted compact-test integration by parts. The conditional PBPS law motivates this prerequisite.
objects.reconstructed: μ is volume.tilted(-W). D is a closable partial real-linear map between scalar and vector L² spaces whose graph consists exactly of almost-everywhere smooth compact gradient pairs. The conclusion concerns the graph of this same D.closure.
objects.evidence: The declaration and blind reconstruction agree on μ, both L² spaces, exact graph witnesses and D.closure. In the supplied module, hsub uses the given D.graph and hmem uses hD.graph_closure_eq_closure_graph; no replacement operator is introduced.

domains.original: The pinned prerequisite is explicitly full-space and finite-dimensional, not the compact weighted-manifold spectral theory cited as background.
domains.reconstructed: E is any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its Borel measurable structure. Integration is over E without a boundary. Dimension zero is not excluded. Tests belong to C¹ with compact support; u and G are L² equivalence classes.
domains.evidence: The theorem's typeclasses and quantified tests match the candidate assumptions. The private helper integrates over unrestricted volume on E. Compactness is required of the test support, not the ambient space. No manifold or boundary theorem is transferred to E.

quantifiers.original: The weighted identity holds for pairs in the completed smooth gradient graph and for compact tests and constant directions.
quantifiers.reconstructed: For every admissible W, every D satisfying closability and the exact graph characterization, every (u,G) in D.closure.graph, every compactly supported C¹ scalar φ and every v in E, both integrabilities and the identity hold.
quantifiers.evidence: These are the quantifiers in the declaration. The graph characterization is an equivalence for all scalar/vector L² pairs. The result is not restricted to the original smooth core. It neither constructs D in this theorem nor proves the converse characterization of closure membership by tests.

assumptions.original: The route paraphrase leaves analytic regularity, normalization and the precise completed-gradient interface implicit; the candidate publication explicitly supplies them.
assumptions.reconstructed: W is C¹ and exp(-W) is volume-integrable. D is closable and has exactly the smooth compact gradient graph. The selected pair belongs to the closure graph, and φ is C¹ with compact support. No curvature, global score bound or differentiability of arbitrary L² representatives is assumed.
assumptions.evidence: All these hypotheses occur in the Lean statement and authored assumptions. The private helper genuinely uses only C¹ W, f and φ plus compact support of φ. Continuity and compact support establish its three volume-integrability obligations. Positivity and integrability of the exponential density justify the finite positive normalization, including in dimension zero.

conclusion.original: Integral φ⟨G,v⟩ dμ equals minus integral u(D_vφ−φD_vW) dμ for completed-gradient pairs.
conclusion.reconstructed: Both displayed integrands are μ-integrable and the same signed weighted identity holds using measurable representatives of u and G.
conclusion.evidence: The signs and directional derivatives agree exactly. The proof establishes genuine integrability with L2.integrable_inner before returning the equality. hPe and hqe transfer between test representatives and the explicit integrands. This rules out merely exploiting the convention for undefined integrals.

scopes.original: An explicitly authored Euclidean analytic prerequisite to the cited route, not a reproduction of PBPS macroscopic coercivity or Kolesnikov–Milman spectral and regularity results.
scopes.reconstructed: A one-way weighted compact-test identity for the given gradient graph closure, without pointwise differentiation of u, unweighted distributional regularity, a full closure-domain characterization, Poincaré, a resolvent theorem or an operator-core theorem.
scopes.evidence: The module introduction, lesson source scopes, final lesson step and blind reconstruction consistently preserve this boundary. The words identifying the same gradient are justified as retention of the same parameter D; they must not be read as proving a converse characterization or independently verifying external resolvent wiring.

constant_dependencies.original: The local identity contains no Poincaré, curvature, spectral-gap or complexity constant; the normalization of the density is implicit in proportionality.
constant_dependencies.reconstructed: Z is the integral of exp(-W), with 0 < Z < infinity. Its reciprocal multiplies both sides and cancels. The conclusion has no quantitative constant depending on dimension, curvature or conditional parameters.
constant_dependencies.evidence: The proof's ht establishes the normalized integration formula and applies it to both sides. P and q depend on φ, v and W and have finite L² norms; no uniform bound for those norms is asserted. No PBPS quantitative estimate is claimed.

publication_boundary: Accepted only as the stated weighted compact-test integration-by-parts prerequisite for the same given completed smooth gradient graph. This does not certify closable-gradient construction, downstream instantiation, reverse weak-gradient characterization, full-space elliptic regularity, a D*D operator core, conditional Poincaré, macroscopic coercivity, Lemma B.1, or either complete paper.
review_evidence: I inspected only the supplied review packet and its cited primary sources, with no prior reviews, registry, plans or repair records. I read the entire supplied module, including private compact_directional_ibp, and all seven authored lesson steps. The helper's product rule, compact-support arguments and three integrability hypotheses support classical full-space IBP. The main proof then normalizes the actual measure, constructs compact L² tests, transfers representatives, proves equality on D.graph, and extends it through a closed equality set of continuous L² pairings. Every authored step matches those proof operations. The exact graph hypothesis is stronger than the forward implication used in hsub, but is openly stated and faithfully retains the intended operator interface. Compilation was reported by the packet; I did not rerun a build or treat that report as semantic evidence. The primary [PBPS Appendix C.1](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.06905v1#A3.SS1) confirms the displayed conditional density, smooth-core density/closed-gradient route and conditional Poincaré use; its later conditional integration by parts is consistent with the local identity. [Kolesnikov–Milman §2.5](https://arxiv.org/html/1310.2526v7#S2.SS5) discusses Sobolev completion and spectral gaps in its compact weighted-manifold setting. That background is not a justification for transferring manifold regularity or spectral conclusions into this theorem.
